Steph — thanks for looping us in. I put together the operational details below and attached a short TAM ops overview and on-call matrix for Argus to include in their appendix. High-level answers: 

• Coverage model (recommended for Regulated Financials): Dedicated TAM + Shared after-hours rotation
  - Primary TAM: named, single point of contact during business hours (Mon–Fri 8am–6pm local)
  - Shared after-hours rotation: small rotation among 2–3 TAMs for urgent follow-ups; Redwood provides the on-call schedule weekly.

• On-call SLAs and escalation windows
  - P1 (Platform down / data loss affecting production): Initial notification acknowledged within 15 minutes; engineering pager escalation within 30 minutes; continuous updates every 30 minutes until mitigated.
  - P2 (Degraded service impacting customers): Initial acknowledgment within 1 hour; remediation cadence and updates every 2 hours.
  - Business-hours support: 08:00–18:00 local business days — direct TAM + engineering triage.
  - After-hours critical coverage: 24x7 for P1 via rotation and direct engineering on-call escalation; non-critical requests queued and addressed next business day.

• Incident communications and templates
  - We provide a SEV1 email template, an incident timeline (T-minus, T0, T+1, T+4), and a postmortem outline.
  - Example: For SEV1 we open a joint incident channel (Slack or Teams), name the incident owner from Redwood and Argus, and publish a public-facing one-line status for customers within 60 minutes where appropriate.

• Evidence for RFP appendix
  - SOC2 primary contact: Priya Natarajan, Security Compliance Lead (security@redwoodinference.com) — (see SOC2-Audit-Contacts.pdf attached).
  - Runbook sample: included as a 1-page summary in TAM_Ops_Overview.pdf.

Attachments (for inclusion in Argus appendix):
  - TAM_Ops_Overview.pdf (overview + runbook summary)
  - oncall_matrix.csv (rotation + escalation points)
  - SOC2-Audit-Contacts.pdf (approved contact list)

Notes / clarifications: 
  - If Argus needs 100% named 24x7 dedicated TAMs (no shared rotation), we can price as a Dedicated Support uplift; default for enterprise regulated customers is the hybrid above.
  - We do not publish full SOC2 reports in RFPs; we share contact names and we can arrange a redacted artifact review under NDA.

Happy to refine — let me know if you want the on-call matrix expanded to include time zones per campus.

—Marissa

Hi James / Sara — thanks for sending the list. Please find our consolidated responses and attachments below. We've kept the appendix short so procurement can paste it directly into the RFP response.

Summary (high level)
• Recommended model for Argus: Dedicated primary TAM during business hours + shared after-hours rotation for critical incidents (can convert to 24x7 dedicated for an uplift).
• P1 SLA: acknowledge < 15 minutes; engineering pager escalation < 30 minutes; updates every 30 minutes.
• P2 SLA: acknowledge < 1 hour; updates every 2 hours.
• Incident comms: joint incident channel, named incident owner, customer-facing status within 60 minutes for SEV1 where appropriate.

Deliverables attached:
- Argus_TAM_Schedule.xlsx (proposed weekly schedule and roster)
- TAM_Ops_Overview.pdf (runbook summary and SEV templates)
- oncall_matrix.csv (detailed escalation matrix)
- SOC2-Audit-Contacts.pdf (SOC2 contact list and redaction guidance)

Next steps:
1) Confirm whether Argus prefers the hybrid model or 24x7 named TAMs — if 24x7 named, we will provide a pricing uplift and updated SLA table.
2) If you want a redacted SOC2 artifact review, we'll schedule a short NDA exchange and a 30-minute walkthrough with our compliance lead.
3) We can tailor the incident playbook to include Argus' internal paging channels (PagerDuty/ServiceNow) — if you send the contact and escalation IDs, we will map them into the oncall_matrix.

If this looks good, I'll prepare a single PDF appendix and a cover email for procurement.

Best,
Steph
